lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: multistep problems using a letter for the unknown quantity
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: multistep problems using a letter for the unknown quantity

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: A school raised $3,200 in September and $2,750 in October, then spent $1,400 on new books. How much remains?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: A charity collected $9459 in the spring and $2102 in the fall, then received an extra $2971 donation. How much money is there in total?
A charity collected $77785 in the spring and $17593 in the fall, then spent $10318 on supplies. How much money remains?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A charity collected $3927 in the spring and $2953 in the fall, then spent $1363 on supplies. How much money remains?
A charity collected $18180 in the spring and $5150 in the fall, then spent $1937 on supplies. How much money remains?
A charity collected $85649 in the spring and $23284 in the fall, then spent $3961 on supplies. How much money remains?
A charity collected $26027 in the spring and $23935 in the fall, then spent $14140 on supplies. How much money remains?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: A charity collected $59829 in the spring and $24178 in the fall, then received an extra $8535 donation. How much money is there in total?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A charity collected $77608 in the spring and $39672 in the fall, then received an extra $17263 donation. How much money is there in total?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
